Richard Nixon

Project 43 · presidential suite · from templates-president/nixon.json · index · repo randomcase/richard-nixon

Republican · 1969–1974 · the American standard: president 4 of the four who managed the war

Role. Vietnamization: began pulling US troops out while shifting the fighting to the South Vietnamese army; widened the air war into Cambodia and Laos; signed the Paris Peace Accords; resigned twenty months before Saigon fell.

Decisions, one line item each

1969-03-18Operation Menu: secret bombing of Cambodia begins, with falsified records.
1969-06-08Midway: first withdrawal of 25,000 announced; Vietnamization named by Laird.
1969-11-03'Silent majority' speech.
1970-04-30Cambodian incursion announced; Kent State four days later.
1971-02Lam Son 719: ARVN into Laos without US ground troops; the test of Vietnamization, failed.
1972-02Beijing; then Moscow in May. The war becomes a detail in a larger deal.
1972-05-08Linebacker and the mining of Haiphong in answer to the Easter Offensive.
1972-10-26Kissinger: 'peace is at hand', twelve days before the election.
1972-12-18Linebacker II, the Christmas bombing, to bring Hanoi back and Thieu along.
1973-01-27Paris Peace Accords signed. Thieu given private letters promising a 'full force' response to violations; Congress never sees them.
1973-08-15Case–Church takes effect: no more US combat in Indochina.
1974-08-09Resigns. The promised response to violations goes with him.

The Joint Chiefs, with their president

Chiefs in office during the term. A chief carried over from the previous president is listed once, with the earlier president, and given nothing more here — only the duty he owed this one, and, where it applies, his last days with him. The Joint Staff, the Pentagon, Arlington, Virginia. The Chairman’s office is on the E-ring, second floor, river side; the Chiefs meet in the “Tank”, Room 2E924, and from 1972 in the Gold Room next to it.

The impeachment

House Judiciary Committee, 1974-07-27 to 1974-07-30.

ArticleChargeVote
IObstruction of justice, the Watergate cover-upadopted 27–11
IIAbuse of power: the IRS, the FBI, the CIA, the Plumbersadopted 28–10
IIIContempt of Congress: the subpoenasadopted 21–17
IVThe secret bombing of Cambodia, 1969–1970, concealed from Congressrejected 12–26 — the one Vietnam article, and the committee would not carry it
VTaxes and the improvements at San Clemente and Key Biscaynerejected 12–26

The war he ran was put to the committee once, as Article IV, and voted down by both parties on the ground that Congress had known enough and funded it anyway. He resigned before the full House voted.

The break, to the Fall of Saigon

1974-08-09 → 1975-04-30 · 264 days

From the resignation to the Fall of Saigon: 264 days. The private letters to Thieu promising a “full force” response to violations were his; Congress had never seen them; Ford inherited a promise with no one to keep it. The break is the interval in which the guarantee behind Vietnamization turned out to be one man.
